prize_parts.citation: for the development of palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the one mature synthetic-methods case on the list with clean attribution. Solving amine and amide binding, beta-hydride elimination and C-N reductive elimination from Pd-amido complexes took new ligand classes, and the result is a general reaction used daily in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. Buchwald and Hartwig each made the catalytic general version, so two names suffice. Base editing is the border-field candidate where I can state what was new chemically: programmable deamination of a single nucleobase without double-strand cleavage, with an adenine deaminase evolved for a substrate no natural enzyme accepts. Liu is the clear driver of both editor families. The pair spans molecule-making and chemical biology and uses exactly three names.
statement.case_against: The 2010 cross-coupling prize makes C-N coupling vulnerable to an extension-of-a-prized-area reading, and Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is an unresolved precursor. For base editing, the 2020 CRISPR prize sits directly beneath it, the chemistry can be read as protein engineering around a known reaction, long-term safety is unsettled, and Nishida and Kondo's concurrent cytidine-deaminase work is a real priority question. A two-part prize with no thematic link beyond 'chemistry' could also be read as bridging first choices. Of the leading ballots, B007 has the widest opening support and I do not claim my pair is the committee centre.

responses.point: He accepts C-N coupling as ubiquitous but weights the 2010 overlap against it and asked how I weigh that overlap against pharmaceutical impact.
responses.response: I weigh it as follows. The 2010 prize recognised C-C bond formation by Pd catalysis. C-N coupling needed different elementary-step solutions, and the answer was ligand design that Buchwald and Hartwig developed separately, which is why it counts as a new capability. Impact is large and visible: the reaction is routine in medicinal chemistry. I accept that a member who values only never-before-possible capabilities will rank it below base editing, and I agree with him that Liu alone is the cleanest credit, so we share B061 even if we differ on the second part.

responses.point: He pairs B001 sequencing-by-synthesis with Liu on a reading-and-rewriting-DNA theme and keeps C-N coupling only as a lower-ranked option.
responses.response: I accept that the reading/writing theme is a more coherent common principle than mine, which is just two different kinds of chemistry. I still cannot support B001 as a part: the 1980 prize already honoured DNA sequencing, the chemically decisive step (reversible terminators) is entangled with instrumentation, and dropping Rothberg, Ju and Mayer invites an attribution fight. A pairing that bridges two members' preferences through a theme is not stronger science than one with clean attribution on both parts. I keep B001 as an alternative.

responses.point: He argues PROTACs make ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis a designable chemical operation, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as a coherent three-person story.
responses.response: The designability argument is persuasive and I treat B007 as the strongest competitor to my B061 part. His own objection decides it for me this year: the cereblon glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Kim, Gray) is a separate mechanistic breakthrough that a Crews/Deshaies/Ciulli citation leaves out, and no degrader is approved. I would move to B007 if a first approval arrived or if the committee settled on a citation and three names that did not look arbitrary.

responses.point: He pairs B007 (Crews, Deshaies) with B061 (Liu) as one achievement on proteins and one on nucleic acids.
responses.response: This is the pair closest to mine in structure, and sharing B061 makes it the likeliest meeting point. I would ask whether Crews and Deshaies alone is defensible when Ciulli's VHL ligands made the approach drug-like and Handa's cereblon work explains the glue branch; a two-name cut works only if the citation is limited to heterobifunctional design. I will not drop B022 for it without a settled B007 attribution, but if the B007 citation is narrowed to the heterobifunctional concept I could accept it as a second part.

responses.point: She did not oppose C-N coupling but would place designed porous catalysts ahead of it because B013 has no earlier prize.
responses.response: I appreciate the fairness. Zeolite design is clearly chemistry and mature, but the cut for a sharp citation is the problem she herself names: Corma, Davis and Zones against Yu, Tsapatsis and earlier unlisted work by Barrer, Breck and Flanigen. C-N coupling has a single reaction with a two-name credit, which gives a precise citation. That precision is why I prefer it, even granting her point that B013 lacks an earlier prize in the area.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 prize and how to treat Kosugi.
Whether base editing reads as chemistry or as a continuation of the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether Nishida and Kondo should be credited.
Whether a first degrader approval or a settled B007 attribution would justify moving to B007 as a part.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My Masamune-school background and stereoselective-methods work are field-adjacent to C-N coupling but involve no personal tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Liu. Linke and Sparr are Lund colleagues with no stake in these candidates. No change since round 1.
